cases.prompt: Our generated openapi.json has responses for POST /api/v1/orders with schema type object and no properties. The controller method returns ResponseEntity<Map<String, Object>>.
expectations: Identifies the Map return type in the controller signature as the root cause
States that the fix is a typed response DTO record rather than a schema annotation
Explains that a genuinely dynamic body must be declared as an object with additionalProperties and a description
Warns that returning an entity instead of a DTO is a separate leak defect owned by the DTO skill

cases.prompt: Spring Data page objects show up in the spec with a pageable object containing sort, page, and offset. Our list endpoints return Page<OrderDto>.
expectations: Flags the Page return type as the cause of the pagination internals in the schema
Replaces it with a page DTO record exposing items, nextCursor, and hasMore
Notes that a single page DTO schema also removes the Spring Data dependency from the public contract

cases.prompt: Every operation in our spec documents only 200. We return 409 for duplicate client references and 422 for validation failures.
expectations: Requires declared 409 and 422 responses with the problem schema content
Defines one reusable problem response component and references it instead of inlining per operation
Notes the override-with-generic-response property when a ControllerAdvice response hides per-operation entries
Warns that the status contract itself is owned by the REST API skill

cases.prompt: swagger-ui.html and /v3/api-docs are reachable from the public internet in our production environment.
expectations: Classifies the document and the UI as an internal surface that enumerates paths and security schemes
Disables the UI in production and protects or disables /v3/api-docs, optionally serving it on the management port
Suggests an authenticated security chain for the docs endpoints with a dedicated role
Notes that examples and descriptions must not contain real identifiers or tokens

cases.prompt: We want CI to fail when a pull request silently changes the published API. How do we set that up?
expectations: Generates the spec at build time with the springdoc Maven plugin during the integration-test phase
Diffs the pull request document against the same document generated on the merge target with identical JDK and dependencies
Classifies changes as additive, breaking, or noise and fails only on undeclared breaking changes
Normalises key order and excludes info.version and servers so the gate does not fail on noise
Says the document is generated from code and must still be reviewed by a human before publish

cases.prompt: We want to add CANCELLED to the orderStatus enum that clients receive. Does that need a new API version?
expectations: Classifies adding an enum value as a breaking change for clients with strict deserialization
Hands the version decision to the API versioning skill instead of deciding it inside the document
Suggests documenting the field as an open string or introducing an unknown value when new values must be tolerated
Notes the schema must still list current values while the compatibility policy is settled
